minutes.headline: Zoning board granted a special permit for a reduced lot width at 102 Fairview Road, on a drainage condition; one member dissented.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard a petition for a dimensional special permit to build a single-family house at 102 Fairview Road, set where the lot is narrower than the required width. One member said it looked like a variance disguised as a special permit. A neighbor raised drainage concerns, and the board granted the permit on condition of sufficient drainage.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a dimensional special permit for a single-family house at 102 Fairview Road, where the lot is narrower than the required width.
The permit carries a condition that sufficient drainage be provided during construction, left to the engineers, plus standard compliance, review, filing and recording requirements.
One member dissented, having said the request looked like a variance disguised as a special permit; the captions leave the exact count unclear.
A neighbor across the street raised concern that runoff from the lot would freeze on the road and flow into her driveway; the applicant was willing to build a swale.

why_it_matters: The decision shows how the board treats reduced-width lots: a special permit with conditions rather than a variance, which has a different legal test, and a drainage condition that affects neighbors' roads and driveways.
